newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First govt would drive dlr, rates lower - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ First govt would drive dlr, rates lower - Peters.

text.p: A New Zealand First-led government would drive down the value of the New Zealand dollar and bring about lower interest rates, party leader Winston Peters said on Sunday.

"We intend to drive that dollar down in the interests of exporters -- the most critical people we need for this country -- and at the same time interest rates will fall back," Peters said on Television One's "Meet the Press" current affairs programme.
Peters was responding to journalists' questions about his party's proposed compulsory savings levy of eight cents in the dollar.

He said he did not underestimate the difficulty some people would have in paying the levy in addition to paying off a mortgage, but said a lower dollar would cause interest rates to fall and make mortgages more affordable.
"That relief will be able to assist them in terms of their long-term savings capacity," he said.
New Zealand was "in hock to international money" and needed to start to finance its own development.
"We do intend to give the cheque back and to take the forest back," he said.
New Zealand First has been running neck and neck with the Labour party for second place behind the ruling National party government in recent political opinion polls.
A general election will be held on October 12.
"Long-term, we have the vision of making ourselves independent," Peters said.
He said New Zealand First's foreign investment policy, which would limit offshore ownership in "strategic" New Zealand assets to 24.9 percent, was non-negotiable.
"We understand the difference between foreign investment and foreign control. Foreign investment should be in our interest, not just in theirs."
He said New Zealand First would reclaim the recently privatised Forestry Corporation from the Fletcher Challenge -led consortium which purchased it.
